title: Ship opum-ward from a lean plugin root carrying only plugin.json and skills/ (DEC-246 a4, 0.1.1)
description:
Filed from WCLI-82 by the ward-cli worker on 2026-10-26, on DEC-246 (a4) relayed by team-lead: the #887 pin merges now, and the lean plugin root is ward-cli's for 0.1.1.

DEC-246 (a4): the opum-ward plugin should ship from a directory that carries only .claude-plugin/plugin.json and skills/, so that installing it fetches nothing. Today the plugin is the repository root: its marketplace entry points at this tree, so an install runs a dependency install that pulls dev tools and a native addon (the keychain binding) along with it. None of that is needed to run the skill, and the skill is all a plugin consumer is asking for.

Scope, as ruled:
- A plugin directory carrying only .claude-plugin/plugin.json and skills/ (skills/ward/SKILL.md today), so a plugin install fetches nothing beyond the skill and its manifest.
- The manifests that name the plugin, its version and its skill path follow it: package.json and .claude-plugin/plugin.json still agree on 0.1.1, and test/plugin-manifest.test.ts is what holds that.
- opum-fleet repoints its marketplace entry at that cut once it exists. That repoint is opum-fleet's change, not this repository's; this task ends when the directory and its manifest exist and the tests pass here.

Not in scope: any change to .github/workflows/release.yml between 0.1.0 and the next cut (see WCLI-91 criterion 2), and any change to the CLI's own behaviour.

Nothing is to be changed for this until 0.1.1 is scheduled: this task records the ruling and its scope so the work is not re-derived. It rides the same cut as WCLI-91 and the two are independent changes.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The plugin ships from a directory that carries only .claude-plugin/plugin.json and skills/, and nothing a plugin install would fetch beyond those.
package.json and the plugin manifest agree on the released version, held by test/plugin-manifest.test.ts.
Installing the pinned plugin in a fresh session resolves the skill from the lean directory, and the install pulls no dependency tree, dev tooling or native addon.
